subject: Editing URL query parameters inside proxy

messages.author: 5d1783676904f45d
messages.subject: Editing URL query parameters inside proxy
parts:
I have a system mostly running that proxies requests to Shiny Server. The reason for this proxy is so that I can run custom authentication (for delivering media through IMS LTI). My proxy lives at https://my-host.com:8080/provider/ and it forwards to Shiny at http://localhost:3838/test/. 

I need to pass information about the user from the authentication step on to Shiny, so I'm trying to edit the request to shiny to include URL parameters that identify the user. However, Shiny seems to ignore the edited request and use the request URI from the original request to the proxy: 

A request to https://my-host.com:8080/provider/?key=value will result in the desired behavior, and session$clientData$url_search shows the query parameter key=value.
A request to https://my-host.com:8080/provider/ in which the proxy changes the URL and opens a new request Shiny shows the session$clientData from the original request, rather than the request that actually goes to Shiny.

messages.author: 5d1783676904f45d
messages.subject: Re: Editing URL query parameters inside proxy
parts:
I've found the reason for this odd behavior. I'll note it here in case anyone else happens upon a similar problem and can't figure out why. 

The pull request that added the URL info to the session$clientData object can be found here: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/pull/122/commits. Looking into the code added by this pull request, I found 

+    // Send initial URL
+    // The hash isn't sent because it can change, and watching for changes can
+    // require polling on some browsers. The JQuery hashchange plugin can be
+    // used if this capability is important.
+    initialValues['.clientdata_url_protocol'] = window.location.protocol;
+    initialValues['.clientdata_url_hostname'] = window.location.hostname;
+    initialValues['.clientdata_url_port']     = window.location.port;
+    initialValues['.clientdata_url_pathname'] = window.location.pathname;
+    initialValues['.clientdata_url_search']   = window.location.search;

This shows that the URL info is populated from the client side; since I was trying to make a proxy which edited the path and query, that information was never communicated to the client. My solution is to have a redirect once authentication is finished. The redirect goes to another access point on the proxy, and includes the query info needed.
